subject: ElevateAI mid-cycle top-up & flexible credit proposal
messages:
From: Ethan Rhodes <ethan@elevate.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie@elevate.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewals planning — quick top-up question

Hi Michael,

Quick question as we plan for Q4: our usage spiked in July and we need roughly +35% more reserved units to maintain latency for customer-facing features. We're mid-contract and want to add capacity without resetting our renewal date.

Sophie asked if Redwood can offer some kind of flexible top-up credit we can purchase now and apply against future committed capacity (we're trying to avoid a large one‑time uplift invoice). Also — any chance of a small volume discount on that top-up or an early-renewal incentive if we co-term at the end of this year?

Attaching our July usage report for context. Can you share options and ballpark economics? We're targeting a decision next week.

Thanks,
Ethan

Attachments: elevate-usage-report-Jul2025.csv
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Rhodes <ethan@elevate.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Sep 2025 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewals planning — quick top-up question

Ethan — thanks for the context and the usage report. Sorry for the delay, I wanted to pull in Ben and Laura to align on pricing/ops.

High level options we can move quickly on:

- Quick top-up (on-demand credits): Buy a block of flex credits at a modest uplift to list and redeem them against Dedicated capacity purchases later. No change to renewal date.
- Pro-rated uplift: Add reserved units to your existing contract prorated to the next renewal period; keeps billing simple but triggers an uplift invoice for the remainder of the term.
- Early co-term + incentive: We can do an early renewal for a 12-month extension with a graduated discount (2–6% depending on commitment size) if you commit to the higher baseline now. This would require legal to sign an amendment.

Ben, Laura — can you confirm feasible discounts for a ~35% mid-term top-up for a $150k annualized ARR account? Also, I think Monica from finance should confirm invoicing cadence if we do flex credits vs pro-rate.

Ethan — I'll send a short proposal (pdf) with numbers by EOD today. If we can get a DocuSign on any amendment, we can apply the new baseline immediately.

Best,
Michael
---
Michael Grant
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Sep 1, 2025 at 08:34 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Ben, Laura — can you confirm feasible discounts for a ~35% mid-term top-up for a $150k annualized ARR account?

We can structure two options that are operationally easy:

1) Flex credits: Customer purchases $X of Flex Credits (applied at a 1:1 token-to-unit conversion) — we offer a 5% purchase discount if they prepay the block and the credits expire over 12 months. Credits do NOT change the committed baseline (keeps renewal untouched). Good for customers who want budget certainty without amending the contract. Minimal legal.

2) Mid-term uplift amendment: Add 35% more reserved units prorated to term end, apply a 7% one-time uplift discount on the incremental capacity if they sign the amendment within 10 business days. This amends baseline so future renewals use the higher baseline. Requires Legal and Procurement sign-off; Monica — can Finance do a single lump invoice for the pro-rated period?

If they want co-term + early renewal (12 months), we can amortize the uplift and push to monthly invoices with a 4% blended discount vs straight uplift.

-- Ben
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Rhodes <ethan@elevate.ai>
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie@elevate.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Sep 2025 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Flex Credits vs Pro-rated Uplift (summary + numbers)

Ethan / Sophie — attached is a short proposal (flex-credit-proposal_v1.pdf) and a contract excerpt showing amendment language. Summary below: 

Option A — Flex Credits (fast)
- Purchase $120,000 in Flex Credits (usable against Dedicated capacity purchases)
- 5% one-time purchase discount applied -> invoice: $114,000
- Credits valid for 12 months, non-refundable, do NOT change renewal baseline
- No legal amendment required; standard SOW/PO accepted

Option B — Pro-rated uplift amendment (baseline change)
- Immediate +35% capacity added, prorated to contract renewal (remaining 4.3 months) -> pro-rated charge: $45,300
- Incremental capacity receives a 7% one-time uplift discount if amendment signed within 10 business days -> invoice: $42,129
- Baseline increases for future renewals; requires signed amendment and legal review (2–5 business days)

Option C — Early co-term (12 months)
- Commit to new baseline now for next 12 months; blended discount 4% across committed units, amortized monthly. Legal amendment + procurement required.

Operational notes: Flex credits are easiest to get out the door quickly; pro-rate is cleaner long-term if Elevate expects sustained usage. Finance (Monica) can do either single invoice (pro-rate) or apply credits to future invoices (flex credits).

Next steps: let me know which option you prefer and I can generate the DocuSign for Option B/C or send an invoice for Option A.

Thanks,
Michael

Attachments: flex-credit-proposal_v1.pdf; elevate-contract-excerpt.pdf
From: Ethan Rhodes <ethan@elevate.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie@elevate.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Sep 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Flex Credits vs Pro-rated Uplift (summary + numbers)

Michael — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. Sophie and I reviewed with finance; two quick notes:

- Flex Credits look attractive because they avoid contract churn and get us capacity fast. Can you confirm credits can be used for both reserved capacity purchases and transient burst capacity?
- If we go Option B (pro-rate amendment) we'd prefer the 7% uplift discount to apply to the full incremental ARR (not just the pro-rated portion) — would Redwood consider that if we sign within 5 business days?

Assuming flexibility on the first point, we want to move forward with Option A today and will follow with a conversation about Option B for long-term planning. Please send the invoice for $114,000 and the redemption instructions.

Appreciate the help —
Ethan
